info.title: CLARION API
info.description: Emergency-first, interoperable health record continuity system.

post.description:
Account-enumeration tradeoff mirrors POST /auth/forgot-password (see
its docstring above): every failure -- unknown email/NRIC or a wrong
password for a real account -- returns the identical generic 401, so
this endpoint can't be used to probe which identifiers have accounts.
The one exception is the lockout response, a distinct 429; that's the
same accepted tradeoff as the forgot-password lockout message -- it
confirms an account exists but nothing more sensitive than that, and it
only ever fires for identifiers that already resolve to a real account
(an unknown identifier just keeps getting the generic 401 forever).

Locked out *by account*, not by source IP alone: IP-based limiting is
weak once this sits behind a shared NAT / Cloudflare tunnel where many
legitimate users can appear to share one IP, and it's trivially
bypassed by an attacker who rotates IPs. This matters most for
staff-issued temp passwords -- handed out in person, but guessable by a
network attacker in the window before the patient's first login and
forced password change. Persisted on the User row (not in-memory), same
as reset_attempt_count/reset_locked_until, so it survives process
restarts and behaves correctly if the backend ever runs multiple
workers.

P1.10 adds LDAP/AD as a second, opt-in (LDAP_ENABLED) provider, staff-only
(see the `ldap_eligible` docstring on _resolve_login_user -- a real
patient NRIC never reaches it, JIT-provisioned or not). Two cases, both
of which then rejoin this same lockout/token-issue flow below:
  - no local User at all, identifier is ldap_eligible -> attempt a full
    bind + role-resolve + JIT-provision (_jit_provision_ldap_user).
  - an existing User with auth_source == "ldap" -> its local
    hashed_password is an unusable placeholder (see
    _jit_provision_ldap_user), so the password check below is replaced
    with a fresh directory bind + role re-sync (_verify_ldap_existing_user)
    instead of ever comparing against that placeholder.
With LDAP_ENABLED unset (the default), ldap_auth.ldap_enabled() is
always False and this function's behavior is unchanged from before P1.10.

Mints a fresh short-lived access token from a still-valid refresh
token, WITHOUT a full re-login -- the web console's silent-refresh
call (cookie-based) and a native client's explicit one (JSON body;
`request.cookies` is simply empty for those, so the `or` below falls
through correctly). See auth.rotate_refresh_token for the actual
validation/rotation/reuse-detection logic; this endpoint is a thin
HTTP wrapper around it plus setting the new cookie.

401 on anything wrong (missing/unknown/expired/reused token) -- same
"nothing more specific than a generic failure" discipline as
POST /auth/login, so this can't be used to fingerprint why a given
refresh attempt failed.

Real server-side logout (Security Audit M4 -- there was none
before): revokes exactly the refresh token this caller presents (see
auth.revoke_refresh_token's "this device only" semantics) so it can
never be used again to mint a fresh access token, then clears the
cookie. Same cookie-or-body source as POST /auth/refresh, for the same
reason (native clients have no cookie jar). Always 200 -- an
absent/already-invalid token is not an error (the caller's intent,
"make sure I'm logged out", is already satisfied); this must never
leak whether a given token was valid.

Act as another role this account holds (nurse -> patient, guard -> patient...). Returns a
fresh access token for that role and remembers it, so the next sign-in starts there. The role
is checked against what the account holds right now; a profile being acted for is dropped.

Staff-only. Creates a patient login if none exists yet, or
regenerates the password of an existing one (this doubles as the
staff-mediated password-reset path — same code, same primitive as a
brand-new issuance). Returns the plaintext temp password exactly once;
it is never stored or logged in plaintext again.

Public, unauthenticated. Step 1 of the two-step email-OTP reset
(replaces the old NRIC+DOB single-step /auth/forgot-password — DOB is
guessable/knowable PII, same weakness as the NRIC it was meant to
supplement, so the product decision was to drop it entirely and prove
identity via a code sent to the patient's own registered email
instead).

Account-enumeration tradeoff (deliberate, carried over from the old
forgot-password design): unknown NRIC, an NRIC with no linked login
yet, and an NRIC/login with no registered email on file all return the
exact identical generic success-shaped response as an NRIC that really
did just get a code emailed to it — a caller cannot distinguish any of
these four cases from the response alone. Whether Mailtrap is even
configured is folded into the same non-signal (see email_service.py) —
a misconfigured deployment must not become externally detectable
either.

The one exception is the request-rate-limit response, a distinct 429 —
same accepted tradeoff this codebase already made for login lockout
and the old forgot-password lockout: "this NRIC is temporarily rate
limited" only confirms a login exists, not medical data or whether an
email is on file, and only ever fires for identifiers that already
resolve to a real account (an unknown NRIC just keeps getting the
generic response forever).

Public, unauthenticated. Step 2 of the two-step email-OTP reset.

Enumeration tradeoff mirrors request-password-reset-otp above: unknown
NRIC, no pending OTP, an expired OTP, and a simply-wrong code all
return the exact same generic 400 -- a caller can't tell "no such
account" from "right account, wrong code" from the response alone.

Authenticated flow for both a forced first-login change
(must_change_password=True) and a voluntary password change.
Deliberately exempt from the must_change_password block enforced by
auth.get_current_user (via get_current_user_allow_pending_change
instead) -- otherwise a user in that state could never call this
endpoint to clear the flag.

post.description:
Lost phone AND recovery codes: an admin clears the user's MFA (they are
prompted to enrol again at next sign-in if their role requires it) and
every session of theirs is revoked. The user is emailed.

Needs the acting admin's own password + authenticator code (step-up), and
never targets the admin's own account -- a sole admin recovers through the
host script (db/reset_admin_password.py --mfa-only).

P3.10: currently-live announcements for one facility
(`starts_at` already passed, `expires_at` NULL or still in the future).
Any authenticated caller may query this -- same "publicly-relevant, not
patient-specific" posture as GET /patients/appointment-slots; management
(unfiltered, admin-only) is GET /admin/announcements.

get.description:
P3.10: bookable slots for a given day (Malaysia-local
`date`, "YYYY-MM-DD"). Any authenticated caller may query this -- it
discloses only which times are free, the same "publicly-relevant
scheduling info" posture as GET /display/{token}. Union of every
matching clinician's free slots (see appointments.py's _clinicians_for)
when clinician_id isn't pinned, so a patient picking "any doctor" still
sees a real, bookable time per row.

Deliberately defined HERE, not on appointments.router (which also
mounts under the "/patients" prefix) -- appointments.router is included
into the app AFTER this router (see main.py), so a literal route
registered there would be shadowed by GET /{patient_id} below matching
"appointment-slots" as a patient_id first. Every literal top-level
/patients/... route (this one, /announcements, /booking-options) must
stay in THIS router, ahead of /{patient_id}, for the same reason.

schema.title: Response List Appointment Slots Patients Appointment Slots Get

get.description:
P3.10: the department + clinician pickers a patient's
self-booking flow needs, at one facility. Same visibility posture as
list_appointment_slots above (and same reason this lives here, not on
appointments.router).

A clinician's profile photo for the self-booking picker (P3.10).
Deliberately as open as GET /booking-options above (any authenticated
user, patients included) -- this is the PUBLIC half of the profile
photo feature; see routers/profile.py::get_staff_photo for the
facility-scoped colleague-only version. Only ever serves a role="clinician"
row -- never leaks another staff member's photo through this path.

New-patient eligibility check against the University's SMP/SMS/e-klinik panel /
Registrar system -- called from the "New Patient"
intake form before/while filling it in. Same role list as create_patient
(this router isn't reachable by `receptionist` by default -- see
permissions.py::DEFAULT_ROLE_PAGES -- and patient creation itself is
already admin/records_officer/clinician only; this check follows that
existing design rather than opening a new carve-out). Advisory only --
see app/campus_registry.py, which this app knows nothing real about, is a
documented mock (2026-09-15), and never blocks patient creation on its
own.

Security Audit H2: default-scoped to patients this user's facility
actually has a relationship to (see _facility_known_patient_ids_select),
never the whole system. `break_glass_reason` is the explicit, audited escape
hatch for a genuine cross-facility need (e.g. a records officer
tracking down a transferred patient's chart) -- unlike
get_patient_full_record's allow-and-log design for a single patient
(no emergency urgency justifies browsing EVERYONE unscoped, so this one
default-denies instead). No admin override on the scoping itself --
admin still needs break_glass_reason like anyone else, consistent with
every other cross-facility guard in this codebase (see
_guard_cross_facility_amend's docstring).

parameters.name: break_glass_reason

schema.description: Supply a non-blank reason to override the default facility scope and browse every patient in the system. Logged prominently (action=list_patients_break_glass) -- use only for a genuine cross-facility need, not routine browsing.

post.description:
Recording a transfer/visit here is what powers the 'what changed since
last visit' transfer view on the web console.

patch.description:
Staff-only edit/correction for an existing encounter (e.g. fixing a
typo'd reason/notes after the fact) -- the POST above stays create-only,
this is what backs an eventual 'edit visit' UI action.

Self-service only, for now: a patient editing their OWN contact
profile (email/phone/emergency contact). No staff-editing variant here
by design -- out of scope for this pass.

full_name / date_of_birth / national_id are immutable via self-service
identity fields: a request that tries to set any of them is explicitly
rejected with a clear 400, not silently ignored, so a caller isn't
misled into thinking an identity-field change actually took effect.

get.description:
Patients (and staff) can review exactly who accessed the record and
when — this is the transparency half of the PDPA-aligned design.

`actor_name` is resolved via a LIVE join against `users.full_name`
(not a value stored/snapshotted on the AuditLog row itself) -- see
models.AuditLog's class docstring for the reasoning: a later name
correction (typo fix, legal name change) should be reflected in old
history too, not stay frozen/wrong. `actor_facility`, in contrast, IS a
snapshot straight off the row (no join needed) -- same docstring covers
why those two fields are deliberately handled differently.

`actor` is only ever a real `users.id` for a staff/patient action --
the "system" actor and the unauthenticated emergency-scan endpoints'
"emergency_responder:<name>" actor have no matching `User` row at all,
so the join is skipped for those (and for a staff `User` account that
has since been deleted, the lookup just degrades to `actor_name=None`
rather than a 500 -- "who" for that row is still available via the raw
`actor` id, just not resolvable to a live display name anymore).

Full document detail, including the (potentially large) raw_text OCR
dump and ai_summary -- deliberately NOT part of _serialize_patient's
'documents' summary list, fetched here on demand instead. Staff-only,
same roles as the AI handover-brief/interaction-check endpoints -- a
patient viewing their own record does not get document detail access in
this pass.

Serves back the original uploaded file (X-ray image, scanned lab
report, etc.) as persisted by POST /ai/digitise/{patient_id}. 404 if no
file was ever persisted for this document (e.g. uploaded before this
endpoint existed) -- only the OCR'd raw_text is available in that case,
via GET /patients/{patient_id}/documents/{document_id} above.

A JPEG preview of a document (P1.7/P1.7b) -- ``size=300`` (default) for
a list thumbnail, ``size=1400`` for a readable "web preview" that avoids
pulling a possibly-15MB original over a slow link. Same roles +
cross-facility visibility gate as GET .../file. An image document is
downscaled; a PDF gets page 1 rendered. 404 when the document has no
stored original or neither applies. The preview is regenerated from the
original on a cache miss, so it is never authoritative and the WORM
original is never touched. Content-addressed (the derived key folds in
the source sha256), so a strong ETag + If-None-Match 304 is safe.

P3.10: a read-only PDF rendered on the fly from an
already-signed Encounter + its ConsultationNote. Deliberately NOT stored
as a ClinicalDocument the way POST /documents/generate's 3 doc_types
are -- there is no free-text/staff-entered content being issued here,
it's fully derived from records that are themselves already immutable,
so regenerating on every request is simpler than a second WORM copy that
could drift from the source encounter. The signature drawn on the page
is the EXISTING per-encounter snapshot taken at sign-off time
(Encounter.signature_object_key -- see models.Encounter's docstring),
not a signature belonging to whoever is downloading -- a patient has no
clinical signature of their own to substitute.

The patient may fetch their own; staff get the same cross-facility
visibility rule as get_patient_full_record (a facility that opted out
of records_shared_publicly can't pull another facility's visit as a PDF
either).

post.description:
P3.5: render a signed Digital Medical Certificate /
Referral Letter / Timeslip as a PDF and file it as a ClinicalDocument --
same WORM bucket, same GET .../file /.../thumbnail serving, same
cross-facility visibility rule as an uploaded scan. REQUIRES a saved
digital signature, same convention as every other sign-off endpoint
here; pass `signature_b64` to save one on the spot.

Unlike the OCR upload path (POST /ai/digitise), a storage failure here
is NOT best-effort -- there is no independently-already-successful OCR
result to preserve, so if the PDF can't be persisted the whole issuance
is rolled back rather than leaving a document row with no file behind
it (same "never store a half-done write" rule imaging.py's medicine-
photo path follows).

Append a signed annotation to one of the patient's clinical
sub-records. Append-only -- there is no update/delete. REQUIRES a saved
digital signature (routers/profile.py); pass `signature_b64` to save one
on the spot if you have none yet.

`resolved` is only valid against a condition and `discontinued` only
against a medication (400 otherwise) -- those two kinds are what the
read path folds into a computed effective_status / effective_active.

get.description:
Every annotation on this patient's records, newest first. Paginated
(code-review follow-up 2026-09-07) with a generous default so the
existing "fetch all" client is unaffected.

post.description:
Called from the patient app (or a guardian acting for a senior citizen)
to (re)issue their emergency QR / physical card.

IMPORTANT design point for your demo pitch: the QR code does NOT encode
medical data. It encodes only a `card_reference` — a pointer. Every scan
mints a fresh, short-lived token via /emergency/scan. This is what
prevents a lost card or a screenshot of the QR from leaking a static
data payload.

A patient is only ever meant to have **one live QR card** at a time —
generating a new one automatically revokes any previous, still-valid
QR grants for this patient first (registered NFC physical cards are
untouched; those are a separate, admin-managed medium — see
/emergency/nfc/register). The count of auto-revoked cards is returned
as `previous_cards_revoked` so the client can tell the user what
happened, instead of silently leaving old QR codes scannable.

Called by an emergency responder's device after scanning the QR or
keying in the physical card's printed reference. No login required —
this is the whole point — but every scan is logged, and only the
pre-approved scope is ever returned. If the caller happens to be a
logged-in staff member, their real identity is bound to the audit
entry (M6); otherwise the typed-in responder name is recorded but
flagged unverified.

A scanner's position that arrived AFTER the scan (slow GPS fix, or the user tapped "share").
Authorised by the one-use `location_token` that scan returned: it only ever reaches the patient
that scan was of, only while the card is still valid, and for an identified scan only from the
same signed-in scanner. Who it is attributed to (tier, role, facility) is what was recorded at
scan time, never what this request claims. The contact gets a "new location" text.

get.description:
Where this patient's card was recently scanned (as reported by the scanners' devices), newest
first. The patient (or a guardian acting for them), or staff at a facility the patient is at.

schema.title: Response List Scan Locations Emergency Locations  Patient Id  Get

get.description:
Read-only status check: "does this patient currently have a live QR
card, and if so what's its reference/expiry?" — with no side effects
(doesn't issue anything, doesn't log an access).

When active, the response also includes `qr_code_base64` — the QR image
is never stored anywhere; it's cheaply re-rendered on every call from
the grant's `card_reference` via `_render_qr_base64`, since the image
content is fully deterministic (`CLARION-EMERGENCY:{card_reference}`).
This is what lets a viewer that *didn't* itself issue the card actually
display it, not just know it exists.

This exists so a viewer that *didn't* itself issue the card (e.g. the
web console, or the same patient reopening the app) can find out a
card was issued/revoked/replaced **elsewhere** (the mobile app, a
different browser tab, etc.) without needing to click "Issue" again.
Poll this endpoint for a "reflects changes made elsewhere" experience
— see web/src/pages/PatientDetail.jsx.

post.description:
Create or update the grant for a physical NFC card's UID. Re-running
this with the same `nfc_uid` (e.g. to fix a typo'd scope, or renew an
expiring card) updates the existing grant in place instead of leaving
an orphaned duplicate — there is exactly one grant per physical card.

No login required — same design as /emergency/scan, but keyed by the
physical card's NFC UID instead of a QR-encoded card_reference. A
logged-in staff caller is bound to the audit entry (M6).

get.description:
Data keys a device caches so it can open an encrypted tag with no
network, plus what it needs to refuse a revoked card offline: the
revocation key and the ids of cards revoked while still unexpired (an
expired card is already refused by the expiry sealed into its record, so
the list stays short). `key_max_age_hours` is how long the device may keep
all of this without a successful refresh. Every fetch is audited.

post.description:
Ingest a device's hash-chained log of offline tag reads. Idempotent
per (user, device, seq) for an identical entry. A *different* entry for an
already-stored seq is a `conflict` (never silently dropped): it is audited
and reported so the client can re-base under a fresh device id. A bad hash
link is stored with chain_ok=False and audited as such.

Revoke by the grant's id (from GET /emergency/nfc/{patient_id}) -- the
raw NFC UID is no longer round-trippable to the client (M7).

get.description:
Staff can see every registered card (scoped to their own facility's
currently-present patients -- see _require_patient_present_for_staff);
a patient can see (read-only) the cards registered to their own
record.

Timeline for one card, newest first, from the audit log. Shows role / organisation /
facility only: a responder's typed name is not repeated here.

Serve one of OUR visits to a registered peer. Unknown/forged callers
and unknown visits all look the same (401/404) to avoid an oracle.

Real-time pre-confirmation safety check (P4.4, tender clause
) for a medication that has NOT been saved yet -- called from
    the Add Medication form before its Save actually persists anything; this
    endpoint itself writes nothing. Screens `drug_name` against the
    patient's current active medications (same pairwise DDI engine as
    GET /ai/interaction-check, incl. the ATC class-level layer) and recorded
    allergies (same check ai/cds_hint.py uses mid-consult), so this and the
    two existing advisory panels never disagree about what counts as a
    conflict.

    Same records_shared_publicly filtering as interaction-check: goes
    through _serialize_patient so an opted-out facility's medications/
    allergies don't leak into the screen.

post.description:
Upload a scanned document (prescription, discharge summary, lab
report). Runs OCR, stores the raw text + a lightweight extraction, and
creates a ClinicalDocument row a human can review before finalising.

Also persists the original uploaded file to the ObjectStore (see the
module comment) so it can be retrieved later via
GET /patients/{patient_id}/documents/{document_id}/file -- previously
the temp file was OCR'd then immediately os.unlink'd, so only the
extracted text was ever recoverable, never the original image/scan
itself. Persistence is best-effort: a storage failure here never blocks
or rolls back the OCR ingestion that already succeeded.

Doctor/staff-published appointment (follow-up visit, procedure, etc.).
Reminder timing is never stored -- see compute_reminder_offsets.

get.description:
Patient (own record only) + clinical staff (admin / clinician /
records_officer -- the same set that can create/modify an appointment).
A receptionist or pharmacist is intentionally excluded even with the
`patients` page: an appointment's reason / precaution_notes / fasting
instructions are clinical detail, not front-desk data. Security Audit
Code-review follow-up 2026-09-07 -- this endpoint previously accepted any authenticated non-patient
token, unscoped and with no cross-facility distinction in the audit log.

Cancelled/completed appointments are included, not hidden -- the client
filters/styles by status (same "don't hide history server-side" stance
as get_audit_log).

schema.title: Response List Appointments Patients  Patient Id  Appointments Get

patch.description:
Staff-only partial update, including the status transition (e.g. to
"cancelled" -- soft-cancel only, matches EmergencyToken.revoked's
pattern; this never hard-deletes a row).

post.description:
Staff-only action that actually moves an appointment's scheduled_at
-- the one place Appointment.previous_scheduled_at/reschedule_reason_*
get written (see models.Appointment's docstring). Used both when a
clinician reschedules unprompted, and after accepting a patient's
reschedule request (POST .../reschedule-requests/{id}/accept) once a
new time has actually been agreed with the patient by phone -- accepting
a request never moves scheduled_at by itself, see
AppointmentRescheduleRequest's docstring for why.

Only valid against a "scheduled" appointment -- rescheduling a
cancelled/completed one would silently resurrect it, which is never the
intent (cancel a stale appointment and create a fresh one instead).

Patient-only, own-record-only: asks staff to reschedule this
appointment. Does NOT move scheduled_at -- see
AppointmentRescheduleRequest's docstring. At most one pending request
per appointment (checked here, not a DB constraint -- see that same
docstring); the patient must wait for staff to accept/reject the
existing one first.

Staff-only. Accepting only records "we'll call the patient to agree
a new time" -- it deliberately does NOT reschedule the appointment
itself; use POST .../reschedule for that once a time has actually been
agreed (see AppointmentRescheduleRequest's docstring for why this is
split into two steps).

Staff-only. The appointment is left exactly as-is -- rejecting is
purely informational for the patient (optionally with clinician_note
explaining why), not a state change on the appointment itself.

Patient self-service booking -- own record only. Reuses the
Appointment table (self_booked=True distinguishes this from a
staff-published appointment, see models.Appointment's docstring) through
a deliberately narrower schema than AppointmentCreate: no reason/
precaution_notes/fasting fields, those stay staff-only clinical calls
(see _APPOINTMENT_STAFF_ROLES above).

The requested scheduled_at is NEVER trusted as a bare value -- it must
exactly match a slot compute_available_slots would currently offer for
the resolved clinician, recomputed here against live data. That check
alone is a read-then-write race, though (two concurrent requests can
both pass it before either commits -- the exact class of bug
models.QueueTicket's docstring warns about for the same reason FastAPI
runs sync `def` routes in a threadpool): the real guarantee is
models.Appointment's `uq_appointments_active_clinician_slot` DB
constraint, caught below as an IntegrityError and turned into a clean
409 -- security-review follow-up, P3.9/P3.10 wave.

get.description:
Facility-wide "what's coming up" view across ALL patients at this
admin's own hospital -- distinct from GET /patients/{id}/appointments,
which is one patient's own history. Defaults to status="scheduled" only
(staff dashboards usually want the upcoming queue, not cancelled/
completed clutter) -- pass ?include_all=true to see full history.

post.description:
facility_name is FORCED to current_user.facility -- MedicineInventoryCreate
has no facility_name field at all, so there's nothing for a client to
override even if it tries to send one in the request body (FastAPI/
pydantic simply ignores unknown keys here, since this schema has no
extra="forbid"). This is the actual security boundary the whole admin
scoping rests on -- see module docstring.

Attach/replace a photo of the medicine or its packaging. Multipart
`file`; max 2MB; PNG/JPEG/WebP/HEIC only (content-type + extension + magic
bytes must all agree). Same action is available to pharmacists via
POST /pharmacy/inventory/{id}/image.

delete.description:
Hard delete -- unlike patient-facing resources this isn't clinical
history worth soft-preserving (an EmergencyToken-style revoked flag
would be pointless here): a discontinued inventory item should just go
away.

schema.title: Response List Inventory Delete Requests Admin Inventory Delete Requests Get

post.description:
Marks the request approved and performs the hard delete of the item.
The item may already be gone (a direct admin DELETE, or a prior
approval) -- that's handled gracefully, the request still resolves.

get.description: The admin approval queue for this admin's own facility, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Purchase Proposals Admin Purchase Proposals Get

post.description:
Approve a pharmacist's purchase proposal and apply it.

- existing item (item_id set): restock it by `quantity` via the shared
  _apply_restock primitive. 409 if the catalogue item has since been
  hard-deleted (a dangling ref -- nothing to restock).
- new item (item_id NULL): create the MedicineInventoryItem
  (quantity_on_hand=0, unit_cost = proposal.unit_cost, barcode =
  proposal.proposed_barcode) then run the same restock for `quantity`.

get.description:
This admin's own facility's settings row, created-on-read with
defaults (records_shared_publicly=True, timezone=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur).

put.description:
Update display_name / address / contact_phone / timezone /
records_shared_publicly for the caller's own facility. Flipping
records_shared_publicly to False immediately hides this facility's
authored clinical sub-records from staff at other facilities (see
routers/patients.py::_serialize_patient); the emergency-scan path and the
patient's own view are never affected.

get.description:
One row per configurable staff role (clinician / records_officer /
receptionist / pharmacist), lazily created with the documented defaults
on first read, plus a read-only `admin` row. `configurable_pages` is the
fixed full column set (["patients","reception","pharmacy"]) so the UI
knows every checkbox that exists.

schema.title: Response Get Role Permissions Admin Role Permissions Get

put.description:
Upsert page access for one role ({role, allowed_pages}) or several at
once (a list -- nicer for a matrix save). Validates that every `role` is
a configurable staff role (admin / patient / emergency_responder are

post.description:
Sets this ticket to `called`. If another ticket at this facility is
already `called`, it is auto-completed first (status -> `done`,

because in real front-desk use, calling the next number IS the signal
that the previous one's turn is over (the receptionist doesn't
separately click "complete" on every ticket before calling the next),
and a hard rejection here would just force an extra click for no real
benefit. A ticket that was actually skipped/no-show is still
distinguishable in the log/audit trail (status transitioned straight
from `called` to `done`, since there is no intermediate "serving"
status), so this doesn't lose information, just avoids an unnecessary
blocking step.

Known, accepted edge case (not a bug, no fix needed): if staff never
call another ticket AND never manually hit Complete/Cancel on the day's
LAST `called` ticket, it's left sitting in `called` state indefinitely
-- there's no background job that auto-closes it. This is harmless: the
Malaysia-local date filter (`queue_date`, see models.QueueTicket) means
it naturally drops off every future day's board on its own, and staff
can still manually complete/cancel it at any time via the endpoints
below. Deliberately not building an "auto-close stale tickets"
mechanism for this -- out of scope for this feature.

"Now serving" is per QUEUE LINE, and a section IS a queue line: calling
the General counter's next number must not auto-close the Emergency
counter's currently-serving patient -- the auto-close only sweeps
tickets in the SAME department (a facility not using sections has every
ticket department=NULL and gets the old facility-wide behaviour).

to record a result manually can do so through the normal sign-off
endpoint regardless.

get.description:
Streams one raw DICOM Part10 file -- the viewer (web/src/components
DicomViewer) fetches every instance of a study this way and hands each
blob to dwv. `instance_id` is checked against the study's OWN stored
instance-id list, never passed through to Orthanc unchecked -- see
models.DicomStudy's docstring.

Static FDI tooth codes + finding/treatment vocabularies -- so the
tooth-chart UI never hardcodes them.

A patient's full tooth-chart history, newest first -- same universal
cross-facility clinical read as patients.py::get_patient_full_record,
MINUS whatever an authoring facility has opted out of public sharing
(HospitalSetting.records_shared_publicly). The hidden-facility exclusion
is applied in SQL BEFORE offset/limit (learned the hard way in P3.1's
review: filtering after pagination under-fills/misaligns pages).

schema.title: Response Get Dental Chart Dental Chart  Patient Id  Get

post.description:
Record + sign one tooth-level observation in a single atomic action
-- same shape as ancillary.py::sign_off_service_request. REQUIRES a
saved digital signature; pass `signature_b64` to save one on the spot.

schema.title: Response List Charge Master Billing Charge Master Get

post.description:
Same facility-scoping rule as ancillary.py::create_catalog_item: a
non-admin's item is always forced to their own facility; an admin may
additionally publish a global item (`facility_name=null`) but never
target an arbitrary OTHER facility.

Append-only, all-or-nothing Excel import into the caller's OWN facility (a global item
still goes through the single-item POST, which keeps that admin-only decision explicit).
`dry_run` defaults to true so a stray call previews instead of writing. Row problems come
back in `errors` with HTTP 200 and nothing is written.

patch.description:
No delete endpoint -- toggle `active` off instead (existing BillItems
FK to this row and must never be orphaned). No admin override: an admin
may edit a global item or their OWN facility's item, never another
facility's private item -- same rule as ancillary.py::update_catalog_item.

get.description:
Facility-local ONLY (Design decision 1) -- always the caller's own
facility's bills, optionally further filtered by patient_id/status.
There is no cross-facility mode for Billing at all, so unlike
ancillary.py::list_service_requests there is no hidden-facility filter
to apply before offset/limit here -- the facility filter below already
runs before pagination, and it's the only filter that matters.

schema.title: Response List Bills Billing Bills Get

post.description:
Voiding is allowed at any bill status except `voided` (correcting a
mistake on an already-finalized bill is legitimate; ADDING a new item
to a finalized bill is not -- see add_bill_item's status guard).

patch.description:
Content fields are PATCH-able only while `status == 'draft'` (Design
decision 4) -- once submitted, further change is a status transition
only (see the submit/approve/reject/void endpoints below, plus the
automatic 'paid' transition in record_payment).

post.description:
"Delete" per the tender -- never a DB delete (Design
decision 4). Any non-paid status may be voided.

get.description:
The field-picker catalogue the Custom Report Builder UI renders
itself from -- one entry per dataset, each with its typed fields
(groupable/filterable flags, enum options).

post.description:
P4.3c NL report narrative: the same selection /reports/run accepts,
turned into a short prose summary by the local LLM -- see
ai/report_narrative.py. Advisory only, nothing persisted.

get.description:
Surfaces real patient names/ids for the high-risk cohort --
    deliberately not run through reporting_engine's anonymize option
: this is a clinical worklist meant to be acted on, not an
    exportable statistical report.

schema.title: Response List Templates Reports Templates Get
Response List Notifiable Disease Reports Reports Notifiable Diseases Get

get.description:
Static CapabilityStatement -- read + patient-scoped search-type on
each resource this façade actually serves. No write interactions
(create/update/delete) are listed because none exist.

Stands in for a real call to the Registrar's system / SMP / SMS /
e-klinik panel. Any NRIC not in `_MOCK_REGISTRY` 404s, same as a real
"not found" from an external directory would.

schema.title: Response Get Kind Reference  Kind  Get

get.description:
Price bands, optionally for one charge_code (a reference_codes product_charges code).
The source has no product -> charge_code link, so this is looked up by code, not per product.

schema.title: Response List Price Tiers Price Tiers Get
Response List Fee Schedules Fee Schedules Get

post.description: An adult with a login of their own lets a carer who already added them act for them.

get.description:
Printable list of the patient's ACTIVE medications. Read-only. Scoped to
patients the caller's facility already deals with (same rule as orders.py:
unknown-to-facility -> 404, never confirms existence); medications from a
facility that does not share its records are left out, as in the record view.

schema.title: Response List Profiles Booking Profiles Get

post.description:
Demo gateway: signs the same event a real gateway would POST to the
webhook and runs it through the same code. Refused on a real provider.

Always goes to the patient's own contact email on file; the caller cannot choose a
recipient, so this cannot be used to send a bill to someone else.

get.description:
Cashier close for one local day (or the `days` days ending on it), in money actually received.

collected = non-voided payments taken in the window, EXCLUDING payments
settled from a deposit (that cash arrived on the deposit day and is counted
there; counting it again when applied would inflate the drawer).
net = collected + deposits received - approved refunds - deposit refunds.
Voids are listed, not netted, so a supervisor reviews them.

parameters.name: day

schema.description: Last day of the range (local); default today
schema.title: Day

parameters.description: Last day of the range (local); default today

get.description: The same figures as /reconciliation, as a printable one-page PDF.

Finalized bills with a balance, aged from finalization. Whole-facility
scan; fine at clinic scale (ponytail: add a SQL aggregate if a facility
holds tens of thousands of open bills).

Mobile update check. Public (no PHI, nothing per-user): the app calls
it on launch and compares against its own version. `latest` drives the
soft "update available" prompt; `min_supported` (optional) drives a
blocking one. Bump CLARION_APP_LATEST_VERSION when a new APK is
published to /get-app.

AdminAppointmentOut.title: AdminAppointmentOut
AdminAppointmentOut.description:
GET /admin/appointments row shape -- AppointmentOut (patient_id is
already on that base) plus patient_name and created_by_name, both
resolved via a LIVE join at read time (same "resolve display names live,
don't snapshot them" reasoning as patients.py::get_audit_log's
actor_name -- a patient's name correction or a staff member's legal name
change shouldn't leave old admin-dashboard rows showing a stale name).

AdminStepUp.title: AdminStepUp
AdminStepUp.description:
The acting admin's own password + current authenticator (or recovery) code,
re-entered before a credential-reset action. `code` may be empty only for an
admin who has not enrolled an authenticator (MFA not enforced for the role).

AdmissionCreate.title: AdmissionCreate
AdmissionCreate.description:
Exactly one of patient_id / national_id must be given -- same
"fail loud if a client bug sends two" idiom as ReceptionCheckinRequest.
If ward_id + bed_number are both given the patient goes to that exact
bed (validated free + gender-compatible); otherwise the backend
auto-assigns (optionally restricted to `floor_id`).

AnalyserResultInboxOut.title: AnalyserResultInboxOut
AnalyserResultInboxOut.description:
P4.8. `result_text` is hl7v2.format_observations' plain-text
rendering of the parsed OBX segments -- a pre-fill for a clinician's
review, never itself the signed result (see models.AnalyserResultInbox's
docstring for why this table has no write path into ServiceResult).

AncillaryStatsOut.title: AncillaryStatsOut
AncillaryStatsOut.description:
GET /ancillary/stats -- the minimal 'Reporting Management: data &
statistics' surface each module clause asks for. Counts are scoped to
the caller's own facility, current open orders + a rolling 30-day
signed-off count, grouped by module.

AnnouncementCreate.title: AnnouncementCreate
AnnouncementCreate.description:
facility_name is FORCED server-side to the acting admin's own
facility -- same "manager admin, not super admin" boundary as
FacilitySectionCreate (see routers/admin.py's module docstring); this
schema has no such field. models.Announcement.facility_name can still
be NULL (global) in principle, but nothing in this API can currently
produce that -- there is no cross-facility "super admin" action here.

AppointmentSlotOut.title: AppointmentSlotOut
AppointmentSlotOut.description: One bookable slot returned by GET /patients/appointment-slots.

AppointmentUpdate.title: AppointmentUpdate
AppointmentUpdate.description:
Partial update for PATCH /patients/{id}/appointments/{appointment_id}.
Every field optional; only fields actually present in the request body
are applied (see model_fields_set / exclude_unset in the router),
matching ConditionUpdate/MedicationUpdate/etc.'s exact pattern.

Deliberately does NOT re-validate the fasting_hours/fasting_required
relationship against just this payload (a PATCH containing only
fasting_hours, with fasting_required already true on the existing row,
is legitimate) -- the router re-checks the relationship against the
MERGED row after applying these fields instead.

BillItemCreate.title: BillItemCreate
BillItemCreate.description:
Body for POST /billing/bills/{id}/items. Exactly one of
`charge_master_item_id` / `service_request_id` /
`medicine_inventory_item_id` must be set, matching `source_type` --
there is deliberately no client-supplied price field anywhere on this
schema (Design decision 2: every BillItem price is server-derived from
the referenced source, never trusted from the caller).

BillingStatsOut.title: BillingStatsOut
BillingStatsOut.description:
GET /billing/stats -- a light facility-level summary, explicitly a
stand-in: the full 'Financial performance reports' clause
is P3.6's job.

BookingAdminSettingsIn.title: BookingAdminSettingsIn
BookingAdminSettingsIn.description:
PUT body. facility_name/display_name/address are accepted (same shape
as GET) but ignored: the facility is always the admin's own and the
display name/address belong to the hospital-settings screen.

BookingAppointmentOut.title: BookingAppointmentOut
BookingAppointmentOut.description:
AppointmentOut plus the facility's display name (both keys carry the
same value: `display_name` matches /booking/facilities items).

BookingOptionsOut.title: BookingOptionsOut
BookingOptionsOut.description:
GET /patients/booking-options -- the pickers a self-booking flow
needs for one facility.

BookingProfilePatch.title: BookingProfilePatch
BookingProfilePatch.description: PATCH: every field optional; only fields actually sent are applied.

CdsHintRequest.title: CdsHintRequest
CdsHintRequest.description:
Whatever the clinician has typed into the SOAP note so far -- never
persisted, this is advisory-only input for ai/cds_hint.py. Same field
names/caps as ConsultationCompleteRequest for consistency, but every
field is optional and unrelated to sign-off.

ChargeMasterItemCreate.title: ChargeMasterItemCreate
ChargeMasterItemCreate.description:
Body for POST /billing/charge-master. A non-admin's item is always
scoped to their own facility regardless of what they send here -- only
an admin may set `facility_name=None` to publish a shared/global item
(the router enforces this, same convention as
ServiceCatalogItemCreate).

ChargeMasterItemUpdate.title: ChargeMasterItemUpdate
ChargeMasterItemUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /billing/charge-master/{id}. No `category`/
`facility_name` change -- same reasoning as ServiceCatalogItemUpdate.

ClaimCreate.title: ClaimCreate
ClaimCreate.description:
Body for POST /billing/bills/{id}/claims. `claim_amount_cents` may
be less than the bill's total -- the copay/split case (Design decision
6) -- the router 400s if it exceeds the bill's current unclaimed
balance (`patient_due_cents`, NOT raw `amount_due_cents` -- a
security-review fix: capping against `amount_due_cents` alone let two
full-amount claims be created against the same bill, since only a
Payment reduces that figure, not a claim).

ClaimUpdate.title: ClaimUpdate
ClaimUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /billing/claims/{id} -- content fields, only
accepted while the claim is still `draft` (Design decision 4).

ClaimVerify.title: ClaimVerify
ClaimVerify.description:
The password is chosen HERE, by whoever proves the inbox -- never at /start, or a stranger
who knows the NRIC + name could overwrite it.

ClockStatusOut.title: ClockStatusOut
ClockStatusOut.description:
Response for POST /staff/clock-in, POST /staff/clock-out, and
GET /staff/clock-status -- always reflects the CURRENT state of the
calling user's own clock, so a client can just re-render the same
widget off any of the three responses.

ConditionUpdate.title: ConditionUpdate
ConditionUpdate.description:
Partial update for PATCH /patients/{id}/conditions/{condition_id}.
Every field optional; only fields actually present in the request body
are applied (see model_fields_set / exclude_unset in the router).

ConsultationMyRoomOut.title: ConsultationMyRoomOut
ConsultationMyRoomOut.description:
Response for GET /consultation/my-room, POST /consultation/session/start
and POST /consultation/session/end. `room` / `tickets` are empty unless
the caller is BOTH clocked in AND holds an active RoomClaim -- same
"withdrawn on clock-out" rule as reception's MyRoomOut.

ConsultationRoomCreate.title: ConsultationRoomCreate
ConsultationRoomCreate.description:
facility_name is FORCED server-side from the acting admin's own row --
this schema has no such field, same forced-facility boundary as
WardCreate / MedicineInventoryCreate (see routers/admin.py docstring).

ConsultationRoomStateOut.title: ConsultationRoomStateOut
ConsultationRoomStateOut.description:
A consultation room as shown on the clinician Consultation page --
identical to ReceptionRoomOut (the room fields + who currently holds it),
aliased so the consultation router has its own named response type.

ConsultationTicketOut.title: ConsultationTicketOut
ConsultationTicketOut.description:
A queued consultation ticket routed to the caller's claimed room, with
the patient's name + DOB joined in so the worklist is readable without a
second call (mirrors ReceptionCheckinResponse's identity-confirmation
fields).

DentalChartEntryCreate.title: DentalChartEntryCreate
DentalChartEntryCreate.description:
Body for POST /dental/chart -- create-with-signature is the sign-off
same shape as ServiceResultCreate. REQUIRES a saved
    digital signature; pass `signature_b64` to save one on the spot.

DentalChartOptionsOut.title: DentalChartOptionsOut
DentalChartOptionsOut.description:
GET /dental/chart-options -- the static FDI tooth codes + finding/
treatment vocabularies, so the tooth-chart UI never hardcodes them.

DicomStudyOut.title: DicomStudyOut
DicomStudyOut.description:
P4.7. `instances` is the list of opaque Orthanc instance ids the
viewer fetches one at a time from
GET /pacs/requests/{request_id}/study/instances/{instance_id}/file --
safe to expose to an already-authorized viewer since that endpoint's own
membership check (against this same list, server-side) is the real
access boundary, not id secrecy.

DispenseRequest.title: DispenseRequest
DispenseRequest.description: Body for POST /pharmacy/dispense: stock down + priced + on the patient's open bill, one transaction.

FacilitySectionCreate.title: FacilitySectionCreate
FacilitySectionCreate.description:
facility_name is FORCED server-side from the acting admin's own row --
this schema has no such field, same forced-facility boundary as
ConsultationRoomCreate / WardCreate (see routers/admin.py docstring).

FloorCreate.title: FloorCreate
FloorCreate.description:
facility_name is FORCED server-side from the acting admin's own row --
this schema has no such field, same forced-facility boundary as
WardCreate (see routers/admin.py docstring). Creating a floor also
creates `ward_count` child Ward rows in the same request.

FloorUpdate.title: FloorUpdate
FloorUpdate.description:
Partial update for PATCH /admin/floors/{floor_id}. Every field
optional; only fields present in the request body are applied (see
exclude_unset in the router). Cross-field consequences (adding/removing
child wards, resizing every child ward, refusing a shrink that would
strand an admitted patient) are all handled in the router against the
merged row -- same technique as WardUpdate.

GenerateDocumentRequest.title: GenerateDocumentRequest
GenerateDocumentRequest.description:
Body for POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents/generate. One flat,
all-Optional field set covering all 3 doc_types (same style as
ConsultationCompleteRequest's SOAP fields) -- the model_validator below
enforces which fields are actually required, keyed on doc_type, so the
error names the missing field instead of a generic 422 shape mismatch.
Free-text fields are capped short enough that the rendered PDF's fixed
single page (app/document_generation.py) never needs to overflow.

HospitalSettingOut.title: HospitalSettingOut
HospitalSettingOut.description:
The caller's own facility's HospitalSetting row (lazily created with
defaults on first GET, same as MedicineBudget).

HospitalSettingUpdate.title: HospitalSettingUpdate
HospitalSettingUpdate.description:
PUT /admin/hospital-settings -- every field optional; only the fields
actually present in the body are applied (exclude_unset in the router).
facility_name is NOT editable here: it's the identity of the row and is
always the acting admin's own facility.

IssueAccountResponse.title: IssueAccountResponse
IssueAccountResponse.description:
Response for POST /auth/patients/{patient_id}/issue-account.
`temporary_password` is shown exactly once — it is never stored or
logged in plaintext anywhere after this response is sent.

LdapRoleMappingUpdate.title: LdapRoleMappingUpdate
LdapRoleMappingUpdate.description: Same validated shape as create -- PUT replaces every field.

MedicineInventoryUpdate.title: MedicineInventoryUpdate
MedicineInventoryUpdate.description:
Partial update for PATCH /admin/inventory/{item_id}. Every field
optional; only fields actually present in the request body are applied
(see exclude_unset in the router), matching ConditionUpdate/
MedicationUpdate/etc.'s exact pattern. Same non-negative validation as
MedicineInventoryCreate, applied to whatever's actually set.

MfaChallenge.title: MfaChallenge
MfaChallenge.description:
POST /auth/login when a second factor is still needed: NO access
token yet. `mfa_enrol` = the account's role requires MFA but it has not
been set up (the client shows the enrolment screen instead of a code box).

MfaTokenWithRecovery.title: MfaTokenWithRecovery
MfaTokenWithRecovery.description:
Returned once when MFA enrolment is confirmed: the session AND the
recovery codes (shown a single time, never retrievable again).

MyProfileUpdate.title: MyProfileUpdate
MyProfileUpdate.description:
Body for PUT /me/profile -- self-service bio + internal contact email.
Full-replace semantics like StaffSectionAssign: both fields are always
written (send null to clear one), neither is a partial patch. Never
touches the login/auth email.

MyRoomOut.title: MyRoomOut
MyRoomOut.description:
Response for GET /reception/my-room. `room`/`tickets` are empty unless
the caller is BOTH currently clocked in AND holds an active RoomClaim --
the "withdrawn on clock-out" rule (see routers/staff.py::clock_out).

NfcRegisterRequest.title: NfcRegisterRequest
NfcRegisterRequest.description:
Staff-only: register (or re-register / update) a physical NFC card
against a patient — for senior citizens / anyone without a smartphone.
Re-registering the same nfc_uid updates the existing grant's scope and
expiry rather than creating a duplicate row.

OfflineTagReadEntry.title: OfflineTagReadEntry
OfflineTagReadEntry.description:
One offline tag read from the device's hash-chained log. `entry_hash`
must equal tag_crypto.read_entry_hash(...) over the other fields.

PasswordResetOtpRequest.title: PasswordResetOtpRequest
PasswordResetOtpRequest.description:
Public, unauthenticated. Step 1 of the two-step email-OTP reset:
identify the account by NRIC alone (dash-tolerant, see nric.py). No DOB
or other guessable PII involved -- proof of identity comes from the
OTP emailed to the patient's own registered address in step 2.

PasswordResetWithOtpRequest.title: PasswordResetWithOtpRequest
PasswordResetWithOtpRequest.description: Public, unauthenticated. Step 2 of the two-step email-OTP reset.

PatientProfileUpdate.title: PatientProfileUpdate
PatientProfileUpdate.description:
Partial self-service profile update. Every field optional; the
router only touches fields actually present in the request body (see
model_fields_set), so omitting a field leaves it unchanged rather than
clearing it. `extra="forbid"` at the model level would reject unknown
keys, but full_name/date_of_birth/national_id are *known* keys we want
a clear, specific error for -- handled explicitly in the router instead
so the error message names exactly which immutable field was sent.

PaymentCreate.title: PaymentCreate
PaymentCreate.description:
Body for POST /billing/bills/{id}/payments. `claim_id`, when set,
links this payment to the Claim it settles -- the router requires the
claim belong to the same bill and `method` be 'insurance' or 'panel'
in that case (Design decision 6).

PharmacySummaryOut.title: PharmacySummaryOut
PharmacySummaryOut.description:
GET /pharmacy/summary -- the two counters the pharmacy console badges
on load. `pending_proposal_count` is this facility's purchase proposals
still awaiting admin review; `low_stock_count` matches BudgetOut's.

PurchaseProposalCreate.title: PurchaseProposalCreate
PurchaseProposalCreate.description:
Body for POST /pharmacy/purchase-proposals -- a pharmacist proposing a
BRAND-NEW catalogue item (item_id is NULL on the resulting proposal).
Restocking an EXISTING item does not use this schema: that goes through
POST /pharmacy/inventory/{id}/adjust with delta > 0, which builds the
proposal server-side from the item.

QueueBoardOut.title: QueueBoardOut
QueueBoardOut.description:
Response for GET /reception/queue -- today's tickets for the calling
staff member's own facility, plus two small computed conveniences so
the queue-board UI doesn't have to re-derive them client-side.

QueueStatusOut.title: QueueStatusOut
QueueStatusOut.description:
Response for GET /reception/queue/status/{patient_id}. Mirrors
GET /emergency/current/{patient_id}'s `{"active": false}` convention
exactly for "nothing to show" -- see routers/reception.py.

ReceptionCheckinRequest.title: ReceptionCheckinRequest
ReceptionCheckinRequest.description:
Exactly one of national_id / patient_id / card_reference / nfc_uid must
be given -- whichever identifier the receptionist actually has to hand.
Validated explicitly (not "silently pick the first non-null one") so a
client bug that accidentally sends two identifiers fails loudly instead
of checking in the wrong patient.

`national_id` is the patient's IC/NRIC (dash-tolerant, resolved against
Patient.national_id -- see routers/reception.py::_resolve_patient); it's
the default front-desk path now that `patient_id` (an opaque internal
UUID) is only a fallback.

ReceptionCheckinResponse.title: ReceptionCheckinResponse
ReceptionCheckinResponse.description:
Response for POST /reception/checkin -- the ticket plus enough of the
patient's identity for the receptionist to visually confirm they
checked in the right person (this endpoint is often reached via a
fumble-prone manual card_reference/nfc_uid entry, so a wrong-lookup
should be obvious immediately, not discovered later).

ReceptionRoomOut.title: ReceptionRoomOut
ReceptionRoomOut.description:
A room as shown on the clinician's "claim a Bilik" list -- the room
plus who (if anyone) currently holds it.

ReceptionStationOut.title: ReceptionStationOut
ReceptionStationOut.description:
Response for GET/POST /reception/station. `qr_base64` is rendered
fresh on every response (same "fully deterministic, never persisted"
approach as emergency.py::_render_qr_base64) -- it's just a rendering of
`token`, nothing else to cache.

ReceptionStationStatusOut.title: ReceptionStationStatusOut
ReceptionStationStatusOut.description:
Response for GET /reception/station when a facility has no active
station yet -- mirrors QueueStatusOut's `{"active": false}` convention.

RecordAnnotationCreate.title: RecordAnnotationCreate
RecordAnnotationCreate.description:
Body for POST /patients/{patient_id}/annotations. `kind` cross-rules
(`discontinued` only for a medication, `resolved` only for a condition)
are enforced in the router, not here, so the error names the target
type. `signature_b64` saves a signature on the caller's profile first if
they have none yet.

RefreshTokenRequest.title: RefreshTokenRequest
RefreshTokenRequest.description:
POST /auth/refresh's optional JSON body -- native-client path only.
The web client relies entirely on the HttpOnly cookie instead and
sends no body at all.

ReportNarrativeOut.title: ReportNarrativeOut
ReportNarrativeOut.description:
P4.3c NL report narrative -- see ai/report_narrative.py. None only
when the local LLM is unavailable/disabled or the report had no rows.

ReportRunRequest.title: ReportRunRequest
ReportRunRequest.description:
Body for POST /reports/run. `dataset` is a key from GET
/reports/datasets; `fields`/`filters`/`group_by`/`sort` are all
optional and validated against that dataset's own field registry by
app/reporting_engine.py (never raw SQL -- see that module's docstring),
so there is no enumerable set of valid field names to check here.

RescheduleAppointmentRequest.title: RescheduleAppointmentRequest
RescheduleAppointmentRequest.description:
Body for POST /patients/{id}/appointments/{id}/reschedule -- the
staff-only action that actually moves scheduled_at. Reuses
AppointmentCreate._check_not_past's exact reasoning: a reschedule to a
time already in the past is almost certainly a typo, not intentional.

RescheduleRequestCreate.title: RescheduleRequestCreate
RescheduleRequestCreate.description:
Body for POST /patients/{id}/appointments/{id}/reschedule-requests --
the patient-only action that files a request for staff to review.

ResponderCreate.title: ResponderCreate
ResponderCreate.description:
Body for POST /admin/responders: a time-boxed community responder
(guard / volunteer) login. `expires_at` is required and capped (see
routers/admin.py::_validated_responder_expiry).

ResponderIssued.title: ResponderIssued
ResponderIssued.description:
Returned once, on creation: the plaintext temporary password is never
stored or shown again.

ResponderUpdate.title: ResponderUpdate
ResponderUpdate.description: Body for PATCH /admin/responders/{id}: move the expiry (extend or shorten).

RoleGrant.title: RoleGrant
RoleGrant.description:
POST /admin/users/{id}/roles. `patient` needs `patient_id` (an existing record with no
login of its own); `emergency_responder` needs `expires_at` (same cap as /admin/responders).

RoomClaimOut.title: RoomClaimOut
RoomClaimOut.description:
One clinician's live claim on a room. `claimed_by_name` is a
read-time join to users.full_name (nullable if the claiming account was
since deleted) -- same live-name-resolution convention as AuditLog's
actor name.

ScanLocationIn.title: ScanLocationIn
ScanLocationIn.description: The scanner device's position. Finite, in range, and not the (0, 0) a failed fix reports.

ScanLocationSend.title: ScanLocationSend
ScanLocationSend.description: POST /emergency/location: a position that arrived after the scan (or needed a tap to allow).

SelfCheckinRequest.title: SelfCheckinRequest
SelfCheckinRequest.description:
Body for POST /reception/self-checkin -- the patient-authenticated
counterpart to staff-run ReceptionCheckinRequest. No patient_id/
card_reference/nfc_uid field: the patient is identified from their own
JWT (current_user.patient_id), never from anything client-supplied.

SelfRegisterCompleteRequest.title: SelfRegisterCompleteRequest
SelfRegisterCompleteRequest.description:
Public, unauthenticated. Final step of self-service registration --
only reachable once the attempt's status is photo_verified (router
enforces this). Same password-length floor as every other
human-chosen-password endpoint in this API.

SelfRegisterStartRequest.title: SelfRegisterStartRequest
SelfRegisterStartRequest.description:
Public, unauthenticated. Step 1 of self-service registration.
No date_of_birth field here (deliberately removed, not deprecated-kept)
-- a standard Malaysian NRIC's first 6 digits already encode the
holder's birthdate, so the router derives the expected date_of_birth
from national_id itself (see routers/self_registration.py::
start_self_registration, via ai/nric_ocr.py::dob_from_ic_number) and
checks it against Patient.date_of_birth as a self-consistency check,

SelfRegisterVerifyOtpRequest.title: SelfRegisterVerifyOtpRequest
SelfRegisterVerifyOtpRequest.description: Public, unauthenticated. Step 2 of self-service registration.

ServiceCatalogItemCreate.title: ServiceCatalogItemCreate
ServiceCatalogItemCreate.description:
Body for POST /ancillary/catalog. A non-admin's item is always scoped
to their own facility regardless of what they send here -- only an admin
may set `facility_name=None` to publish a shared/global item (the router
enforces this, not this schema).

ServiceCatalogItemUpdate.title: ServiceCatalogItemUpdate
ServiceCatalogItemUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /ancillary/catalog/{id}. No `module`/`facility_name`
change -- moving an item between modules or facilities is a new item, not
an edit (same reasoning as everywhere else immutable-identity columns
stay off the PATCH schema).

ServiceRequestCreate.title: ServiceRequestCreate
ServiceRequestCreate.description:
Body for POST /ancillary/requests -- the 'order'. `source_encounter_id`
is required when `source == 'physician_order'` (checked here so the 400
fires before any DB work) and ignored otherwise.

ServiceResultCreate.title: ServiceResultCreate
ServiceResultCreate.description:
Body for POST /ancillary/requests/{id}/result -- performs AND signs
off in one atomic action (same shape as
routers/consultation.py::ConsultationCompleteRequest). REQUIRES the
caller to already have a saved digital signature, or pass
`signature_b64` to save one on the spot.

StaffProfileUpdate.title: StaffProfileUpdate
StaffProfileUpdate.description:
Body for PATCH /admin/staff/{user_id}/profile -- identical shape to
MyProfileUpdate, admin-editing a colleague's bio/contact_email instead of
their own.

StaffRosterEntryOut.title: StaffRosterEntryOut
StaffRosterEntryOut.description:
One row of GET /admin/staff -- a clinician/records_officer at the
admin's own facility, plus their live clock status. Duplicates (rather
than nests) the clocked_in/since/last_clock_out_at fields from
ClockStatusOut -- keeps this a single flat shape for the roster table,
with no client-side unwrapping of a nested object needed.

StaffSectionAssign.title: StaffSectionAssign
StaffSectionAssign.description:
Body for PATCH /admin/staff/{user_id}. `section` is required in the
payload (send explicit null to un-assign) -- a section string must be
the name of an ACTIVE FacilitySection at the admin's own facility, else
400 (see routers/admin.py::assign_staff_section).

StockAdjustRequest.title: StockAdjustRequest
StockAdjustRequest.description:
Body for POST /pharmacy/inventory/{item_id}/adjust. `delta` > 0 is a
restock (accrues procurement spend at `unit_cost` or the item's stored
unit_cost); `delta` < 0 is a dispense/consume (no budget effect).

SwitchRoleRequest.title: SwitchRoleRequest
SwitchRoleRequest.description: POST /auth/switch-role: act as another role the account holds.

WaitingRoomDisplayCreate.title: WaitingRoomDisplayCreate
WaitingRoomDisplayCreate.description:
Body for POST /admin/waiting-room-displays. `section` (optional) pins
the screen to one FacilitySection's queue; omitted / null = whole
facility. `show_full_names` opts this one screen out of the default
masked patient labels.

WardUpdate.title: WardUpdate
WardUpdate.description:
Partial update for PATCH /admin/wards/{ward_id}. Every field
optional; only fields actually present in the request body are applied
(see exclude_unset in the router). Deliberately does NOT re-validate the
total_beds/occupied_beds relationship against just this payload (a PATCH
containing only occupied_beds, against a row whose existing total_beds
already accommodates it, is legitimate) -- the router re-checks the
relationship against the MERGED row after applying these fields instead,
same technique as AppointmentUpdate's fasting_hours/fasting_required
cross-field validation.
